subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — evidence stamp & approval loop
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — evidence pack & proposed 6-month pilot

Hi Emily — thanks for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a recommended path to get the AWS private offer active quickly while preserving your procurement team's ability to validate security and billing. High-level proposal: 

- Offer structure: 6-month pilot (convertible to 12-month at month 5) at $0.045/token equivalent (pilot discount applied)
- Activation: AWS private offer (seller guided) — buyer PO + basic evidence pack required to satisfy activation checklist
- Buyer approvals we expect: Procurement + Finance (CFO signoff on annual conversion)

To speed the AWS intake team, we propose shipping a compact evidence stamp: a three-doc bundle that AWS accepts for activation checks — an SOC 2 summary, the DPA excerpt, and a short Mutual Action Plan with procurement contact + PO template. Attaching a draft of the Mutual Action Plan and an SOC2 summary for your review.

Requested from your side:
1) Procurement contact name/email for PO routing
2) Any corporate PO wording constraints (billing address, remit-to)
3) If you prefer to start on a 12-month firm term instead of the 6-month pilot

If greenlit, I can run this through our AWS activation playbook and pre-validate the evidence bundle with the AWS intake team to avoid back-and-forth.

Attachments: PrivateOffer_MaintenancePlan_v1.pdf (proposal), SOC2_Type2_Summary.pdf (evidence stub), Greenline_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (mutual action plan)

Thanks — I’ll hold off on formalizing the private offer until I hear your preference on term length.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodai.com
Mobile: +1 415-555-0198

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — evidence pack & proposed 6-month pilot

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. A couple quick notes from procurement: 

- We typically push for 12 months for marketplace deals, but we might accept a 6-month pilot if there is clear conversion language and no refund complexity. Our CFO will want to see forecasted spend for the 12mo conversion.
- Evidence stamp sounds good; procurement will still ask for the full SOC 2 report during legal review but the summary is fine for AWS intake.
- PO wording: we require a standard billing address and a single remit-to line (I’ll paste the standard language once I confirm).

Can you confirm whether the pilot price is fully billable (no credits) and if there’s an automatic conversion clause or opt-in? Also we have a network security contact who will ask a couple of quick questions about data residency — can you include an option note about region routing (us-east vs customer region)?

If it helps, I can loop in Martin Huang (our integrations lead) on the technical gating.

On timing — we’d like to move fast and have procurement sign the PO this month if the evidence pack and conversion language are in order.

—Emily
Emily Carter
Director, Procurement | Greenline Health
emily.carter@greenlinehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: AWS Marketplace private offer — Greenline (procurement asks + evidence stamp)

Vanessa / Ben — forwarding Emily’s note. She’s open to a 6-month pilot only if conversion language is very clear and finance sees the forecast. Procurement will ask for full SOC2 later but AWS intake is OK with a compact summary for activation. Quick asks for internal alignment: 

1) Do we want to offer a 6-month pilot convertible to 12mo with an explicit conversion price and no early-termination credits? (my recommendation: pilot price billable, with an opt-in conversion at month 5 that invoices at the pre-agreed annualized rate)
2) Can finance pre-approve the conversion MO? We need a quick stamp so procurement can sign without looping the CFO mid-activation.
3) Legal: I’ll keep legal out for the first activation pass but we’ll need a short DPA excerpt. Is the SOC2 summary PDF acceptable to AWS intake or do we need a signed attestation?

If you both sign off I’ll: (a) pre-validate the three-doc evidence stamp with AWS intake, (b) send the Mutual Action Plan to Emily with explicit conversion language, and (c) prepare the private offer draft for signature.

TL;DR: need a fast greenlight on pilot->convert approach and finance pre-approval on conversion mechanics.

—Jonas

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS Marketplace private offer — Greenline (procurement asks + evidence stamp)

Jonas — Ben here, finance side. I reviewed the numbers and we can pre-approve the conversion mechanics with the following constraints: 

- Pilot is fully billable; no refundable credits.
- Conversion opt-in window opens at month 5 and must be exercised in writing by the buyer; if exercised we invoice the remaining prorated annual amount at the agreed annual rate.
- If the buyer does not opt in by day 150 we automatically let the pilot expire (no automatic conversion).

These terms keep billing predictable for revenue recognition. I also confirm the pilot price is acceptable from a margin perspective at the proposed volume band for Greenline. Vanessa — if legal is comfortable with the DPA excerpt, we’re cleared to proceed with pre-validation to AWS intake.

Jonas — please send Martin (cc’d by Emily) the technical note about region routing. I’ll review final HubSpot deal terms before you mark the offer as active.

—Ben
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
